commits.title: Every admin text area has its module: the 49 that were missing, written by a script from admin-text.ts

changes.how: A one-off generator, plain Node, run from the repo root. It reads src/lib/admin-text.ts as text. From each import line of the form 'import { <x>En, type <X>Messages } from "./admin-messages/<stem>.en";' it learns the file stem and the English constant; from each entry of the CATALOGUES object, '<area>: { en: <x>En, nb: <x>Nb },', it learns the area's key and its two constants (67 entries today). For every area that has no module yet under src/lib/admin-words/ it writes src/lib/admin-words/<stem>.ts. The content copies, token for token, the shape of a module step 0.7 wrote (open src/lib/admin-words/sign-in.ts or any other file there first, and src/lib/admin-area.ts for the reader's name and type). If 0.7 followed the review's design the file is: import type { AreaWords } from "../admin-area"; import { <x>En } from "../admin-messages/<stem>.en"; import { <x>Nb } from "../admin-messages/<stem>.nb"; then a doc comment naming the area, then export const <area>Words: AreaWords<"<area>"> = { area: "<area>", words: { en: <x>En, nb: <x>Nb } };. The script prints the list of files written and exits 1 if an area in AdminAreaMessages has no CATALOGUES entry or an import it cannot match. It writes nothing else.

Written by the script above: one file for each of the areas 0.7 did not cover (49 of 67 if 0.7 made 18; ls src/lib/admin-words | wc -l must print 67 afterwards, plus any index or test file 0.7 put there). Do not hand-edit them. No file may carry 'use client' and none may import anything but its two catalogue files and the type from admin-area.

The file is src/lib/admin-area.ts (made by step 0.7). Keep what 0.7 exported (the type AreaWords<A> and the reader areaText(lang, a), which returns a.words[lang]). Add the reader for several areas, used where adminTexts() is used today: export function areaTexts<const T extends readonly AreaWords<AdminArea>[]>(lang: AdminLang, areas: T): Pick<AdminAreaMessages, T[number]["area"]>, returning Object.fromEntries(areas.map((a) => [a.area, a.words[lang]])) cast to that type. Types come from './admin-text' and './admin-lang' by import type only: this file must have no value import at all (check: rg -n '^import (?!type)' --pcre2 src/lib/admin-area.ts prints nothing).

Build CATALOGUES from the area modules so each area's two files are still named in one place while callers move: replace each entry '<area>: { en: <x>En, nb: <x>Nb },' by '<area>: <area>Words.words,' with one import per area from './admin-words/<stem>', and turn every 'import { <x>En, type <X>Messages } from "./admin-messages/<stem>.en";' into 'import type { <X>Messages } from "./admin-messages/<stem>.en";' and delete the '<x>Nb' imports. adminText() and adminTexts() keep working unchanged. Add above CATALOGUES: 'Going away (bloat review step 2.25): read an area through its module in src/lib/admin-words and areaText(); this table is deleted when no caller is left.'

Test support only: export const ALL_AREA_WORDS, an array of all 67 area modules' exports, typed so that leaving one out does not compile: declare const check: { [A in AdminArea]: AreaWords<A> } built as an object literal with every area as key, and export ALL_AREA_WORDS = Object.values(check). Only test files may import this file.

It imports adminText and adminTexts from './admin-text' (line 4) and walks every area for equal keys in both languages. Change it to walk ALL_AREA_WORDS from '@/test/admin-words-all' with areaText(lang, a) and areaTexts(lang, [...]); every existing assertion stays, and the count of areas it walks stays 67 (add expect(ALL_AREA_WORDS).toHaveLength(67) if the file has no such count).

Widen its rule: a module with 'use client' (and any module such a client module value-imports) may not value-import a file of src/lib/admin-words/ either; an area module holds both languages. Read the test first and add the folder to the pattern it already uses for src/lib/admin-messages; keep its allowed exceptions as they are.

commits.title: A codemod moves adminText() and adminTexts() calls to the area's module, starting with src/components/admin

changes.how: Plain Node, run as 'node docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/admin-words-codemod.mjs <folder> [--write]'. It builds the map area -> { stem, export name } from the files of src/lib/admin-words. For every .ts and .tsx file under <folder> that is not a test: (1) replace each call that matches /\badminText\(\s*((?:[^(),]|\([^()]*\))+?)\s*,\s*"(\w+)"\s*\)/g by 'areaText($1, <area>Words)'; (2) replace each 'adminTexts(<lang>, ["a", "b", ...])' whose second argument is an array literal of string literals (may span lines) by 'areaTexts(<lang>, [aWords, bWords, ...])'; (3) add 'import { areaText } from "@/lib/admin-area";' (and areaTexts when used) and one 'import { <area>Words } from "@/lib/admin-words/<stem>";' per area used, sorted, after the file's last import of an '@/lib/' module, never twice; (4) remove adminText and adminTexts from the file's import of '@/lib/admin-text' (or './admin-text'), keeping type imports from it (AdminArea, AdminAreaMessages, ClientArea and the like) as 'import type { ... }', and delete the import line when nothing is left. Leave untouched, and print as 'by hand: <file>:<line>', every call it cannot match: a second argument that is not a string literal, and adminTexts() with a named constant (EDITOR_AREAS, PLATFORM_SITE_AREAS). Refuse to write a file whose first 300 characters hold 'use client' and print it: a client module must not import an area module. Without --write it only prints what it would change.

Run the codemod with --write on src/components/admin (44 files call adminText today: rg -l 'adminTexts?\(' src/components/admin -g '!*.test.*'). Then by hand, in this folder: the places where English words are a default. Find them with rg -n 'adminText\("en"|areaText\("en"' src/components/admin: scheme-preview.tsx line 17 (words: w = adminText("en", "bookings").schemePreview), data/export-forms.tsx line 16 and data/findings-table.tsx line 15 (a module constant EN), inventory/stock-import-views.tsx line 97 (a default parameter), wishlist-admin.tsx line 16 (ENGLISH()). In each, delete the English default and make the words a required prop or parameter; then fix every caller the type checker reports by passing the words the page already has in the account's language (areaText(lang, bookingsWords).schemePreview and so on). A test that relied on the default passes the English words itself, imported from the catalogue file.

Only its header comment: it says the admin's words come from adminText(lang, area) on the server; reword to areaText(lang, <area>Words) with the module in src/lib/admin-words. The scan itself counts English in markup and does not change.
